title: Session Masking and Evidence SLA — vendor exhibit (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This exhibit is intended to be an attachable schedule to the main Data Processing Agreement (DPA) or Master Services Agreement. It defines vendor obligations, SLAs, and evidence packaging related to short-lived session data generated when Redwood Inference customers send queries to vendor-hosted inference endpoints ("session events" or "session logs"). The focus is on runtime masking/redaction, retention limits, deletion evidence, and audit artifacts that support customer and regulator requests.

Quick summary (tl;dr):
- Vendor must implement session-level masking for PII-sensitive tokens and optional full-session redaction for identified customers.
- Maximum retention for raw session logs: 72 hours by default, configurable to 0–90 days by contract.
- Vendor must produce cryptographically-signed deletion receipts and an evidence bundle within 10 business days of request or scheduled purge.
- Audit sampling: quarterly sample pull + one full-scope annual evidence package for enterprise customers.

Draft clauses (language for insertion):
1) Definitions (abbreviated)
- "Session Event": any discrete inference request and the associated ephemeral metadata, response tokens, KV cache traces, and routing identifiers generated while processing a single customer request.
- "Masking": deterministic or probabilistic token transformation applied at pre- or post-processing to remove or obfuscate PII or other sensitive content.
- "Evidence Bundle": a signed archive containing deletion receipts, retention logs, redaction rulesets, and hashes of purged artifacts.

2) Runtime Masking Requirement
Vendor shall implement and maintain reasonable technical and organizational measures to mask or redact PII in Session Events. Masking shall occur as close to ingress as possible (pre-tokenization preferred) and shall be designed to avoid altering response semantics unless explicit redaction is requested. Masking modes include:
- token-scrubbing (pattern-based),
- named-entity redaction (NER-driven),
- customer-provided regex/plugin masking, and
- full-session redaction (drop entire input payload+response but preserve telemetry).

3) Retention and Purge SLA
Vendor will retain raw (unmasked) Session Events for no longer than 72 hours by default. For customers requiring stricter retention, Parties may agree to shorter retention (including immediate discard) at contract signature. Customer may set per-project retention via the Console API.
Purge process: scheduled hourly purge jobs with audit logging. Completed purge operations must be reflected in retention logs within 24 hours.

4) Deletion Receipts and Cryptographic Proofs
When Session Events are purged (scheduled or ad hoc), Vendor shall generate a deletion receipt that includes: unique purge job id, epoch timestamp (UTC), list of session identifiers (or hashed identifiers), storage shard identifiers, and a SHA-256 hash of the pre-purge artifact manifest. Vendor shall sign the deletion receipt with a vendor-managed key and provide the signed receipt to Customer on request within 10 business days.

5) Evidence Bundle and Audit Access
For audit requests (customer or regulator):
- For routine audits, Vendor will provide quarterly sampled Evidence Bundles within 15 business days.
- For enterprise full-scope audits, Vendor will provide a complete Evidence Bundle within 30 business days (or an agreed timeline).
Evidence Bundles will include: retention logs, purge receipts, masking/ruleset versions (redacted for vendor-sensitive internals), configuration snapshots for the relevant timeframe, and cryptographic manifests enabling integrity verification.
Vendor will not provide plaintext copies of unmasked customer data in Evidence Bundles except under mutually agreed procedures and with additional safeguards (escrow, secure room, or on-prem witness).

6) Incident and Suspected Retention Violations
If Vendor discovers or is notified of a retention policy violation impacting Customer data, Vendor shall:
- Notify Redwood Inference Security within 48 hours of discovery;
- Freeze relevant retention/purge schedules to prevent further propagation;
- Produce an interim Evidence Bundle (preliminary receipts, affected session ids, scope estimate) within 7 business days;
- Propose remediation and estimated customer notification timeline within 10 business days.

7) Sampling, Testing, and Certification
Vendor agrees to quarterly sampling of retention/purge jobs (sample size: min 0.5% of daily sessions or 500 sessions, whichever is smaller) and to publish a short report (masked) showing purge success, average latency to purge, and any anomalies.
Redwood reserves the right to commission an independent third-party technical assessment of retention and masking controls once per 12 months, subject to mutually agreed NDA and scope.

8) Termination and Forensics
On contract termination, Vendor will perform an end-of-contract purge of remaining Session Events within 5 business days and deliver a final Evidence Bundle. If Customer requests a forensic extraction prior to purge, Vendor will provide a secure, time-limited access mechanism (e.g., S3 presigned URL with additional MFA) and will log all downloads with signed receipts.

Operational notes / implementation guidance (engineering-friendly):
- Masking close to ingress: implement as a standalone filter stage in the request pipeline (pre-tokenizer). Keep transformations idempotent and versioned.
- Retention logs: use append-only ledger with (time, shard, job id, session hash, masking-version) rows. Keep for 1 year for audit purposes (masked values ok).
- Purge job id: UUIDv4; store job lifecycle events (created, started, finished, verified).
- Deletion receipts: store signed receipts in a separate immutable store and expose via API with throttling.
- Evidence packaging: produce zipped bundles including human-readable summary + machine-readable JSON manifests + PGP/PKCS7 signatures.

Open questions / items to resolve before legal review:
- Default retention: is 72 hours acceptable for Hosted API? (Product suggests 24 hours for PLG tiers, 72 hours for enterprise trials).
- Masking semantics vs. model quality: how to commit to "avoid altering response semantics" in contract language without compromising vendor safety?
- SLA credits for evidence delivery delays: what penalty model if Vendor misses a 10 business day receipt delivery?

Checklist for next steps (owners):
- [Ava] align with Product on default retention tiers and Console controls (due 2024-11-20).
- [Daniel] prototype deletion receipt schema and signing mechanism, produce sample JSON (due 2024-11-28).
- [Priya] validate that proposed sampling rates are feasible operationally (due 2024-12-04).
- [Marta] draft red-lined insertion into DPA for legal review (target 2024-12-12).

References and related docs:
- Confluence: session-masking-design (link above)
- JIRA: JIRA-SEC-789 (retention engine workstream)
- Prior templates in drive: kept for reference but this exhibit diverges by focusing on receipts and cryptographic evidence.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on evidence delivery timelines — infra can potentially produce receipts faster; want legal buffer.
- Keep an eye on performance impact of pre-token masking — suggest we do a POC that measures 95th percentile latency increase before binding contract language.
- We should be careful not to commit to deletion of replicated backups unless we can ensure irrecoverability (see backups/snapshot policy).

End of draft.

Unresolved:
- Sample JSON for deletion receipt (todo by engineering).
- Exact SLA credit amounts and how to compute them.

[internal: do not share outside Redwood/vendor partnership until redlined DPA is approved]
